item.text:
Research was completed for Chapters 2B–8B. No scores were assigned.

Persistence was unavailable: the read-only worker could not write `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following append-only handoff must be applied by the parent process. Existing IDs E001–E031 are preserved.

### Chapter 2B

- **E032** — Refugees International’s October 2022 field research reports rising Rohingya-camp insecurity, APBn deployments, mass arrests, alleged APBn abuse/extortion, and weak investigation/accountability. Locators: sections “Rising Insecurity,” lines/paragraphs 110–124. Target-period; institutional Bangladesh responsibility, not personal orders. Contrary evidence: increased security presence and temporary lulls in attacks. Maps: `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`, `3B.6`, `6B.3`.
- **E033** — The same field report records improvements in camp roads, drainage, fire response, wastewater treatment, and e-vouchers. Locator: sections “Current Situation,” paragraphs 99–101. Positive humanitarian/security-capacity evidence, jointly attributable to Bangladesh, UN agencies, donors, and NGOs. Maps: `2B.7`, `2B.10`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`.
- **E034** — Bangladesh’s 2022 Joint Response Plan documented a coordinated government–UN refugee response for January–December 2022. Locator: UNHCR document record, title and plan-period description. Formal coordination evidence, not proof of effective implementation. Maps: `2B.7`, `2B.10`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `8B.6`.

Shortfall remains on external-force initiation, procurement rationale, military-harm investigations, and proxy conduct. Myanmar shelling was treated as external context, not Bangladesh aggression.

### Chapter 3B

- **E035** — The U.S. 2022 Human Rights Report records 81 disappearance cases under UN Working Group review; government information was insufficient to establish victims’ fate or whereabouts. Locator: PDF pp. 4–5, paragraphs on WGEID. Target-period institutional evidence; no personal command attribution. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.10`.
- **E036** — The report also records security-force torture allegations and the use of remand custody. Locator: PDF p. 5, torture/remand section. Adverse institutional evidence, with allegation status preserved. Maps: `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`.
- **E037** — The UK FCDO 2022 report records 70 deaths and 6,914 injuries connected to political events, while also reporting 31 extrajudicial killings and 21 abductions by year-end. Locator: paragraphs 934–939. Adds a target-year denominator and contrary decline signal. Maps: `3B.2`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`.
- **E038** — The FCDO report states Odhikar’s NGO registration renewal was denied in June 2022. Locator: paragraphs 939–940. Supports retaliation/monitoring-access concerns; attribution is administrative and institutional. Maps: `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `4B.6`, `7B.7`.

The denominator remains incomplete and independent remedies or command-chain findings were not recovered.

### Chapter 4B

- **E039** — Bangladesh’s Election Commission issued a September 2022 roadmap identifying 14 challenges, including administrative neutrality, black money, muscle power, law and order, and public confidence in electronic voting. Locator: Business Standard, paragraphs 150–158. This is direct 2022 EC-operation evidence, but it also documents unresolved institutional risks. Maps: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`.
- **E040** — Access Now/#KeepItOn reporting cited by The Daily Star recorded six Bangladesh internet shutdowns in 2022, reportedly around BNP rallies; the government and BTRC denied issuing shutdown instructions. Locator: paragraphs 197–218 and 224–226. Target-period evidence with explicit attribution dispute. Maps: `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`.
- **E041** — The U.S. religious-freedom report records constitutional equality guarantees alongside minority complaints about harassment, violence, and insufficient punishment of perpetrators. Locator: 2022 International Religious Freedom report, Bangladesh section. Supports minority-equality gap without attributing every incident to Hasina. Maps: `4B.7`, `4B.10`, `3B.10`.

Judicial independence, succession conduct, and appointment records remain unresolved.

### Chapter 5B

- **E042** — World Bank results reporting states that Bangladesh’s e-GP system processed 80% of public procurement expenditure in FY2021, reduced procurement time, and preserved bid, award, and complaint records for audit. Locator: paragraphs 67–87. Positive institutional-reform evidence with World Bank and government co-attribution. Maps: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`.
- **E043** — The World Bank’s Spring 2022 Development Update records 6.2% headline and food inflation by February 2022, with marginalized households facing food inflation more than twice the official rate. Locator: PDF p. 8, paragraphs 224–256. Adds distributional adverse evidence and a real-income caveat. Maps: `5B.2`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`.
- **E044** — Bangladesh’s Anti-Corruption Commission investigated alleged contract violations in procurement of ten Bangladesh Railway locomotives in June 2022. Locator: Daily Star report dated 30 June 2022. This is an investigation, not a corruption finding and not evidence of Hasina’s personal involvement. Maps: `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`, `7B.8`.
- **E045** — The IMF 2022 Article IV materials identify persistent financial-sector vulnerabilities, low revenue, and need for structural reform. Locator: IMF Country Report No. 22/71, Bangladesh sections on financial-sector vulnerabilities and reform. Institutional adverse context; no personal nexus. Maps: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `8B.7`.

No verified 2022 contract-level personal benefit, asset concealment, or professional-appointment evidence was found.

### Chapter 6B

- **E046** — UNICEF reports that 20 months of COVID school closures led Bangladesh’s Education Ministry to create a remote-learning and emergency-continuity strategy, including television, radio, digital, and printed materials for 150,933 marginalized children. Locator: UNICEF Bangladesh case study, “About” section. Positive correction and resilience evidence. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`, `8B.6`.
- **E047** — The World Bank reports ROSC II reached 735,000 disadvantaged children, half girls, including rural, urban-slum, and Rohingya children, with monitoring and certification systems. Locator: paragraphs 34, 68, 75–81, 97–98. Positive distribution and implementation evidence, jointly attributable. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`, `8B.6`.
- **E048** — UNICEF’s Bangladesh education survey found rural participation in remote learning was 15.9%, versus 28.7% in urban areas. Locator: survey findings summary. Contrary distributional evidence showing unequal access. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`.
- **E049** — Refugees International reports only 248,000 Rohingya children had reached the Myanmar Curriculum Program, while refugees and humanitarian actors questioned teacher qualifications and educational quality. Locator: paragraphs 125–138. Target-period service-quality evidence; responsibility shared with donors and humanitarian providers. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`.

Affordability, health-service quality, and durable neutrality remain weakly evidenced.

### Chapter 7B

- **E050** — The 2022 Railway procurement investigation is retained as a bounded integrity-relevant institutional event only. It does not establish Hasina’s personal benefit, dishonesty, favoritism, or concealment. Maps: `7B.5`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`.
- **E051** — World Bank reporting records procurement safeguards including online bid evaluation, bidder validation, audit preservation, and complaint tracking. This is contrary evidence against treating the entire procurement system as wholly unregulated, but it does not establish personal integrity. Maps: `7B.5`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`.

The personal-integrity gap remains material. No authenticated asset declaration, beneficial-ownership record, sworn statement, independent personal financial investigation, or verified corrective statement was recovered.

### Chapter 8B

- **E052** — World Bank reporting states that 4,550 Union Parishads adopted formula-based central grants, annual audits, performance assessments, and more predictable local financing. Locator: paragraphs 34, 68–79. Positive implementation and coordination evidence. Maps: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.
- **E053** — Save the Children’s 2022 post-flood assessment found that disaster magnitude exceeded community preparedness and response capacity, despite local-authority delivery and recovery efforts. Locator: assessment abstract, paragraphs 35–36. Contrary crisis-management and adaptation evidence. Maps: `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.
- **E054** — The World Bank’s Independent Evaluation Group found that Bangladesh engagement during FY2011–20 produced long-run progress but also implementation delays, weak readiness, staffing problems, and procurement constraints in complex sectors. Locator: IEG evaluation/blog, “Implementation and Results” discussion. Useful contrary evidence against equating programs with successful execution. Maps: `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`, `8B.10`.
- **E055** — The 2022 IMF staff-level agreement records an explicit reform program addressing macroeconomic stability, external vulnerability, social spending, climate spending, and financial-sector governance. Locator: IMF press release, paragraphs describing the October–November 2022 mission and program objectives. Positive goal-setting evidence, not proof of completion. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.

### Manifest corrections required

The parent manifest should:

- change **E025** from `final_evidence` to `discovery_only`, preserving its mappings `["1B.2","1B.3","1B.7"]`;
- preserve **E023** as `context` unless the parent has authenticated independent support for its self-reported licensing claims;
- preserve **E031** as Chapter `1B` only; its later accidental `2B` expansion and unrelated methodology mappings should be removed;
- append E032–E055 with the mappings above;
- retain all existing IDs and exact prior lens mappings.

The main recoverable improvements are new 2022 evidence for Rohingya security/accountability, disappearance denominators, Election Commission planning, internet shutdowns, procurement implementation, distributional inflation and education gaps, local-government delivery, and flood-response limitations. Personal financial integrity, command-chain responsibility, judicial independence, and durable ruler-specific execution remain unresolved.
